subject.title: [Bug]: Sandbox container exits immediately when no-new-privileges is applied (exec /usr/bin/sleep: operation not permitted)

question: Should OpenClaw support a Docker sandbox `no-new-privileges` opt-out or fallback for hosts where the flag causes container startup EPERM?
rationale: The failure blocks sandbox sessions, but disabling or retrying without this Docker hardening option changes the sandbox security boundary and likely adds config, fallback, or diagnostic behavior that should be chosen intentionally.

options.title: Explicit dangerous override
options.body: Add a documented `sandbox.docker` opt-out that defaults to the current hardened behavior and reports weakened sandbox posture in status, doctor, and security audit surfaces.

options.title: Diagnostic-only fix
options.body: Keep the flag mandatory and improve startup/status errors so operators can identify the host-level Docker incompatibility without changing sandbox hardening.

options.title: Tightly detected fallback
options.body: Retry without the flag only for a narrowly detected startup EPERM and record the runtime as weakened for audit and status visibility.

recommendation.title: Explicit dangerous override
recommendation.body: Add a documented `sandbox.docker` opt-out that defaults to the current hardened behavior and reports weakened sandbox posture in status, doctor, and security audit surfaces.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest current history signal around the Docker sandbox architecture and security/config boundary touched by any real fix.
